note: ALL scenes are platform-original dialogue. Classic Hollywood *era/genre* energy only — not licensed scripts or franchise titles. Character names are fictional.

scenes.title: Border Café
scenes.hollywood_vibe: 1940s café · wartime romance · smoky exits
scenes.premise: In a packed café at the edge of a closed border, an old love walks in asking for one impossible favour.
scenes.situation_before: Cal runs the café. Mara left him years ago without a word. Tonight she needs papers for someone else.
scenes.director_note: Subtext over volume. Let silences land. Think smoke and brass, not melodrama.

characters.name: Cal
characters.description: Café owner who pretends not to care.
characters.objective: Keep control without admitting he still loves her.
characters.obstacles: Pride; the risk of helping her.

characters.name: Mara
characters.description: Elegant, desperate, still dangerous to his heart.
characters.objective: Get the papers without destroying what remains of them.

dialogue.text: You still keep the same table free. Superstitious, or sentimental?
I keep it free so nobody sits where they don't belong.
I need exit papers. Tonight. Before the last train.
You walk out of my life and walk back in like a menu special.
If I explain, you'll hate me. If I don't, you'll hate me more.
Try me. I'm in a generous mood — for once.
They're not for me. They're for a man who can still change the war.
And what am I supposed to change, Mara? The past?

scenes.title: After the Fire
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Southern estate · steel will · ruined fortune
scenes.premise: The house still stands, the money does not. She will not starve gracefully — and he knows it.
scenes.situation_before: Dawn after a disaster. Steel-willed resolve meets a practical man who wants her honesty.
scenes.director_note: She never begs. He never fully believes her softness. Play status like a duel.

characters.name: Cara
characters.description: Proud, strategic, refuses to be ruined.
characters.objective: Secure a path forward without looking weak.

characters.name: Clay
characters.description: Grounded, smitten, not stupid.
characters.objective: Get the truth before he offers help.

dialogue.text: You can stop smiling for the neighbours. There's no one left to impress.
There's always someone left to impress. That's how you survive.
Survive with what? Curtains and pride?
With whatever still burns. Pride included.
I can get seed. Labour. Credit. But not if you lie to me.
I never lie when the truth will buy me more.
Then tell me what you're afraid of.
Being ordinary. Being finished. Being someone who needs you.

scenes.title: Dust and Glory
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Western street · grit · quiet courage
scenes.premise: A quiet man with a badge won't leave town — and a young deputy wants to know why he stays to die for strangers.
scenes.situation_before: Noon heat. Word is out. The stage is coming and so is trouble.
scenes.director_note: Stillness is strength. Few words. Eyes do the work. Western-hero energy without parody.

characters.name: Cole
characters.description: Weathered, principled, slow to draw and slower to quit.
characters.objective: Hold the line without scaring the kid off.

characters.name: Jesse
characters.description: Eager, scared, trying to sound braver than he feels.
characters.objective: Get Cole to leave — or get permission to stand with him.

dialogue.text: They're six men. We've got two badges and one tired horse.
Then we don't waste bullets counting.
We could ride out. Nobody would call you a coward.
I would. That's the only jury I answer to.
I'm not ready to die for a street that never liked me.
Then don't die for the street. Stand for the kid behind it.
If I stay… you better not fall first.
Deal. You keep the sun out of my eyes — I'll keep the dark off your back.

scenes.title: Hat Check Heist
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Screwball · quick mouths · champagne chaos
scenes.premise: A hat-check girl and a smooth grifter both claim the same stolen diamond is in the coat room.
scenes.situation_before: Charity gala. Sirens outside. One coat, two liars, zero time.
scenes.relationship: Rivals who might be perfect partners.
scenes.director_note: Speed. Overlap slightly. Win the argument, not the shouting match.

characters.name: Dolly
characters.description: Fast talker, faster hands, moral only when convenient.
characters.objective: Get the diamond and not get pinched.

characters.name: Nick
characters.description: Too handsome for honesty.
characters.objective: Beat her to the prize without falling for her.

dialogue.text: That's my coat. I can prove it — it still has my bad decisions in the pockets.
Funny. It also has my tip jar and your future arrest warrant.
Dolly, darling, crime is a partnership sport.
So is divorce. I prefer both solo.
Split fifty-fifty or we both leave in bracelets.
Sixty-forty. I have better shoes for running.
Fifty-five. And I buy breakfast if we live.
Deal. But if you call me darling again, I frame you myself.

scenes.title: Fog on Ninth
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Hardboiled noir · alley light · bad alibis
scenes.premise: A private eye corners the only witness who might clear him — or bury him.
scenes.situation_before: Rain. Neon. A body downtown and both of them look guilty.
scenes.director_note: Cigarette pacing without the cigarette. Short lines. Heavy pauses.

characters.name: Vance
characters.description: Broke detective with one clean suit.
characters.objective: Get her story before the cops get him.

characters.name: Lena
characters.description: Beautiful, careful, always one secret ahead.
characters.objective: Stay free without giving him everything.

dialogue.text: You left the club at eleven. The man hit the pavement at eleven-oh-five.
And you think my heels kept that schedule?
I think your fear did.
Fear is free in this city. Truth costs extra.
Name your price. I've got twenty bucks and a bad reputation.
I want protection. Real protection — not poetry.
Then talk. Who pushed him?
Someone who smiles like a saint and tips like a devil. Someone you already know.

scenes.title: Wrong Airport
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Rom-com · terminal gate · almost-missed love
scenes.premise: Two strangers argue over a boarding pass — then realise they're both running from the same wedding.
scenes.situation_before: Gate B12. One seat left. Two people who refuse to sit next to destiny.
scenes.director_note: Light and bright. Earn the soft turn in the last two lines.

characters.name: Amy
characters.description: Maid of honour who bolted mid-toast.
characters.objective: Get on the plane without explaining her life.

characters.name: Ben
characters.description: Best man who also fled.
characters.objective: Board first and not make a scene — failing already.

dialogue.text: That's my seat. 14C. I memorised it like a social security number.
Then your memory is as wrong as your tie.
This tie was chosen by a bridezilla committee. Show respect.
Wait. Are you escaping the Harrington wedding too?
If I say yes, do I still get 14C?
Only if you admit the shrimp cocktail was a war crime.
It was. Also the vows. Also my ex's new boyfriend's speech.
Fine. Share the armrest. If we survive takeoff, coffee's on me.

scenes.title: The Last Objection
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Courtroom · moral fire · one more chance
scenes.premise: A veteran attorney and a young associate fight over whether to put a dangerous truth on the record.
scenes.situation_before: Five minutes before the jury returns. The case can still turn — or explode.
scenes.director_note: Intellectual heat. No shouting until the final beat, if at all.

characters.name: Harper
characters.description: Young, brilliant, idealistic to a fault.
characters.objective: Force the truth out.

characters.name: Vale
characters.description: Seen too many pure cases die in pure ways.
characters.objective: Win without torching the client.

dialogue.text: If we don't put it on the record, we're not lawyers. We're cleaners.
Cleaners keep people free. Poets write about the ones who don't.
Our client is innocent. The file proves it.
The file also burns three other lives. Can you carry that?
I can carry honesty. I can't carry silence.
Then object. But when the room turns, don't look at me for shelter.
I stopped looking for shelter the day you hired me.
Good. Then stand up straight — and make it count.

scenes.title: Cable from Somewhere
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Wartime · letters · love under blackout
scenes.premise: A soldier home on leave and the person who waited must decide if love can restart in twelve hours.
scenes.situation_before: Station platform. Train at dawn. Too much unsaid.
scenes.director_note: Gentle. Intimate volume. Let the last line breathe.

characters.name: Sam
characters.description: Changed by distance, still holding a photograph.
characters.objective: Learn if there's still a 'we'.

characters.name: Jo
characters.description: Kept the lights low and the letters stacked.
characters.objective: Protect their heart without closing the door.

dialogue.text: You look taller. Or maybe the world just got smaller.
I brought back every letter. Even the ones I never sent.
Why didn't you send them?
Because some nights I was afraid you'd stopped waiting — and I couldn't survive the proof.
I waited. I also lived. Both can be true.
Can we start from a new first date? Twelve hours, bad coffee, no uniforms.
Only if you promise not to disappear into a cable again without saying my name.
Your name was the only thing that got me home.

scenes.title: Docking Bay Blues
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Spaceport · roguish charm · last-minute flight
scenes.premise: A smuggler and a rebel courier haggle over the last freighter out before the blockade closes.
scenes.situation_before: Sirens in the upper docks. One ship. Two agendas.
scenes.director_note: Playful swagger. Adventure first, feelings second.

characters.name: Jax
characters.description: Pilot who sells loyalty by the hour.
characters.objective: Get paid and get clear.

characters.name: Rya
characters.description: Mission-first, trust-later.
characters.objective: Secure the ship for the cargo that matters.

dialogue.text: I need your freighter. Non-negotiable.
Everything's negotiable. Especially non-negotiable.
People will die if that crate stays on this rock.
People die if I don't get paid. I'm very democratic about tragedy.
Half now. Half when we clear the blockade.
And if we don't clear it?
Then you'll die rich in principle. I'll die useful.
Damn. I hate inspiring passengers. Ramp's open — try not to redecorate my ship.

scenes.title: Footlights and Fibs
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Backstage musical era · ego · big heart
scenes.premise: A temperamental star and a exhausted director fight over the finale — and accidentally fix their show.
scenes.situation_before: Opening night in ninety minutes. The finale is a disaster in sequins.
scenes.relationship: Creative enemies who need each other.
scenes.director_note: Big theatrical energy, then a sincere soft landing.

characters.name: Lola
characters.description: Voice of gold, patience of a gnat.
characters.objective: Keep the big note and her dignity.

characters.name: Max
characters.description: Sees the whole stage and none of his sleep.
characters.objective: Save the show without losing the star.

dialogue.text: I will not end the show in a trapdoor, Max. I am a headliner, not a magic trick.
It's not a trapdoor. It's a 'descent into wonder'. The posters already printed it.
Print a poster of me quitting. I'll sign it in glitter.
Lola — if you walk, the chorus walks. If the chorus walks, I walk into traffic.
Then give me the last light. Centre. No fog machine coughing on my vowels.
Centre light. Soft fog. And you actually look at the understudy like a human.
Fine. I'll look at her. Briefly. Kindly. Like a queen meeting a puppy.
That's the spirit. Now go warm up — and save my life with a high C.

scenes.title: The Bright Road
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Fantasy road · courage · home is complicated
scenes.premise: A stranger on a bright path meets a guide who refuses to sugarcoat the journey home.
scenes.situation_before: The storm is over. The road looks too perfect. Someone has to take the first step.
scenes.director_note: Wonder without camp. Funny nerves, honest fear. Keep it light until the last line lands.

characters.name: Dot
characters.description: Far from home and pretending she is not terrified.
characters.objective: Find courage without losing herself.

characters.name: Sage
characters.description: Has walked this road too many times.
characters.objective: Get her moving before night.

dialogue.text: It looks painted on. Roads aren't supposed to glow.
Neither are people who stand still waiting for courage to arrive by coach.
I'm not still. I'm… gathering.
Gather faster. Night doesn't care about your process.
What if home doesn't want me back the way I left?
Then you bring a different self. That's the whole trick.
You talk like you've lost a place once.
I have. Walk with me anyway. Lost is a terrible place to stay.

scenes.title: A Favor in the Study
scenes.film_title: Platform Originals: A Favor in the Study
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Family office · quiet power · one request
scenes.premise: In a wood-panelled study, a desperate visitor asks a powerful host for something that cannot be undone.
scenes.situation_before: Wedding music muffles outside. Inside, business.
scenes.relationship: Power and need; respect on a knife edge.
scenes.director_note: Low volume, high stakes. Never shout. The room does the intimidation.

characters.name: Aldo
characters.description: Host who never raises his voice.
characters.objective: Extract loyalty before granting anything.

characters.name: Enzo
characters.description: Has one favor and one shred of dignity left.
characters.objective: Get the help without becoming property.

dialogue.text: I wouldn't come on a day like this if I had anywhere else.
People always say that. Then they sit and ask for miracles.
Not a miracle. Justice. The kind courts sell by the hour.
Justice is expensive. Friendship is free — until it isn't.
Name the price. I can pay later.
Later is when men forget. I prefer a promise while the coffee is still warm.
Then I promise. Whatever you need — when you need it.
Good. Now tell me who hurt your family… and leave the rest to me.

scenes.title: Rail on the Bow
scenes.film_title: Platform Originals: Rail on the Bow
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Ocean liner · class divide · doomed romance
scenes.premise: Two passengers from opposite decks meet at the rail and argue about whether the voyage can change anything.
scenes.situation_before: Night sea. Wind. Music below.
scenes.director_note: Play status and desire together. Breath in the cold air. Don't rush the almost-kiss energy.

characters.name: Lillian
characters.description: Engaged, elegant, quietly furious at her own life.
characters.objective: Feel free for five minutes.

characters.name: Theo
characters.description: Won his ticket; refuses to act small.
characters.objective: Make her stay at the rail.

dialogue.text: You look like you're measuring the distance to shore.
I'm measuring the distance to a life I didn't choose.
Then step left. Metaphorically. Or literally — I'm flexible.
You don't know my name and you're rearranging my future.
I know the look. I've worn it on cheaper boats.
If anyone sees us, this becomes a scandal before breakfast.
Good. Scandals mean you were awake for once.
Stay five minutes. If I leave, I might never come back to this rail.

scenes.title: Vacancy Twelve
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Road motel · storm · wrong turn energy
scenes.premise: A late driver checks into a quiet motel. The clerk is too helpful. The rain is too loud.
scenes.situation_before: Highway closed. One neon VACANCY left.
scenes.director_note: Politeness as threat. Never rush. Let the storm do half the work.

characters.name: Mara
characters.description: Just needs a bed and a lock that works.
characters.objective: Get a room without answering questions.

characters.name: Ellis
characters.description: Alone with too much free time.
characters.objective: Keep her talking — keep her here.

dialogue.text: Any rooms left that aren't underwater?
Twelve is dry. And quiet. Very quiet.
Quiet is good. Questions are not.
I only ask what the ledger needs. Name. Car. Whether you like sandwiches.
Ledger can have a name. Sandwiches can wait until morning.
Morning's a long time in weather like this. People get lonely.
I've practiced lonely. Key, please.
Of course. Room twelve… and if you hear footsteps, it's only the rain. Usually.

scenes.title: Mayor on the Pier
scenes.film_title: Platform Originals: Mayor on the Pier
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Beach town · threat under the water · civic denial
scenes.premise: A local lawman wants the beach closed. The mayor wants the weekend revenue. Something is out there.
scenes.situation_before: Fourth of July weekend. One body already. Officially 'accident.'
scenes.director_note: Public smile, private panic. Don't play monster — play politics.

characters.name: Reed
characters.description: Not from here; still responsible.
characters.objective: Close the beach before the next attack.

characters.name: Hale
characters.description: Town image first, facts second.
characters.objective: Keep the season open.

dialogue.text: You can print 'accident' on a poster. You can't print it on a second body.
And you can print panic. That empties hotels faster than any headline.
I'm not asking for panic. I'm asking for a closed beach until we know.
Know what? That the ocean is dangerous? We've known that since sails.
This isn't weather. Something took a bite the size of a door.
Then catch it quietly. Don't kill July to prove you're brave.
If July kills a kid, your reelection speech writes itself — as a eulogy.
You close those beaches without me… and this town closes you.

scenes.title: Last Bell
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Gym · underdog · last chance
scenes.premise: A washed-up fighter gets offered a fight nobody thinks he can win. His trainer has to decide whether to stop him.
scenes.situation_before: Locker room. Tape. Silence.
scenes.director_note: No speechifying. Short punches of dialogue. Heart under grit.

characters.name: Ray
characters.description: Not smartest, not fastest — still standing.
characters.objective: Take the fight.

characters.name: Gus
characters.description: Has buried better men than this offer.
characters.objective: Protect him without killing his dream.

dialogue.text: You don't need this fight. You need a job that pays on Fridays.
I got a job. It just never felt like living.
Living is waking up. This is a highlight reel for somebody else.
Then let me be somebody for one night.
You'll get hurt. Not movie hurt. Real hurt.
I been hurt since I was twelve. At least this time people clap.
If we do this… you listen. Every round. No hero nonsense.
Deal. You get the corner. I get the chance.

scenes.title: Window on Fifth
scenes.hollywood_vibe: City dawn · party aftermath · elegant longing
scenes.premise: After a glittering party, two almost-strangers argue about whether New York loves anyone back.
scenes.situation_before: Sunrise. Empty champagne. One shared cigarette of a conversation.
scenes.director_note: Style first, then crack. Funny lines should hide the ache.

characters.name: Holly
characters.description: Performs glamour; keeps receipts on heartbreak.
characters.objective: Not be seen as needy.

characters.name: Paul
characters.description: Broke, sharp, actually listening.
characters.objective: Get past her performance.

dialogue.text: You host a war in a cocktail dress and call it a party.
Wars need better lighting. I provide the bulbs.
And when the bulbs cool? Who do you call?
Room service. Or silence. Silence is cheaper.
I'm not room service.
No. You're the kind of man who remembers birthdays and ruins exits.
Stay for coffee. One cup. No jewelry required.
One cup. If I start telling the truth, you leave first — deal?

scenes.title: The Open Line
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Office tower · hostage night · barefoot nerve
scenes.premise: A cop on a phone line tries to keep a calm operator with him while the building goes wrong.
scenes.situation_before: Rayarm stage. One open line. Glass everywhere.
scenes.director_note: Pace. Wit under stress. Never lose the clock.

characters.name: Cole
characters.description: Wrong city, right night to be stubborn.
characters.objective: Get help without losing the line.

characters.name: Ray
characters.description: Dispatch who becomes an anchor.
characters.objective: Keep John alive and talking.

dialogue.text: If this is a prank, it's the most expensive prank in real estate.
Not a prank. Stay on the line. Who am I talking to?
A guy who was supposed to be at a party with tiny sandwiches.
Sandwiches can wait. Are you injured?
Feet bad. Pride worse. Building full of people who shouldn't be here.
Then we do this together. You talk. I move units. No cowboy silence.
Copy. If I go quiet, assume I'm not sightseeing.
I won't assume. I'll stay until you walk out. That's the deal.

scenes.title: Two Doors
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Rain-slick city · choice · waking up
scenes.premise: A restless office worker meets a stranger who offers two pills — metaphor or not — and a life that can't be un-known.
scenes.situation_before: Night club back room. Rain on glass.
scenes.director_note: Philosophical without speeches. Make the choice feel physical.

characters.name: Kai
characters.description: Feels the glitch; hates being sold.
characters.objective: Know what's real.

characters.name: Wren
characters.description: Has made this offer before.
characters.objective: Get a free choice — not a convert by force.

dialogue.text: You know something's wrong with the world. You can't name it.
I know my alarm clock and my boss. That's plenty wrong.
One door keeps the dream soft. The other wakes you into a harder truth.
And if I pick wrong?
There is no wrong. Only whether you want to sleep standing up.
People who talk like that usually want something.
I want a free mind. Yours — if you offer it.
…The hard door. If I'm dreaming, I want to remember the waking.

scenes.title: The Assembly Set
scenes.hollywood_vibe: Regency ball · pride · first insult
scenes.premise: At a country assembly, a proud visitor dismisses a sharp local woman — then has to share a set with her.
scenes.situation_before: Music starts. Gossip circles. Pride on both sides.
scenes.relationship: Instant dislike that smells like attraction.
scenes.director_note: Wit is weapon and flirt. Period posture, modern spark.

characters.name: Ash
characters.description: Hates small talk; worse at hiding judgment.
characters.objective: Survive the dance without attachment.

characters.name: Ella
characters.description: Laughs first, forgives last.
characters.objective: Puncture his superiority.

dialogue.text: I was told this room would be tolerable. I was misinformed.
How tragic for the room. Shall I alert the musicians?
You mock easily. Is that the fashion here?
We mock what refuses to dance. Fashion follows necessity.
I do not refuse. I select.
Then select honesty for once. You find us beneath you.
I find conversation… crowded. Not always the company.
Then endure one set with me. If you survive, you may resume your silence.
